blocks.text: This is the most widespread land ecosystem of Pakistan's plains, with xerophytic (drought-resistant) plants whose thorns deter herbivores and reduce water loss.

blocks.alt: A simple labelled landscape of a tropical thorn forest beside an information card.
blocks.caption: The tropical thorn forest: a labelled schematic and fact card (original diagram).
blocks.long_description: A flat, sunny plain with scattered thorny shrubs. The card gives the location (Indus plains of Punjab, Sindh and western Balochistan), climate (arid to semi-arid, 200-750 mm of rain, summers up to 50 C), plants (jhand, peelu or wan, karir, kikar), animals (camel, houbara bustard, chinkara, golden jackal, gerbil, porcupine) and status (heavily degraded by settlements and canal-irrigated farming).

blocks.caption: Profile of the tropical thorn forest
rows: the Indus plains: much of Punjab (Bahawalpur, Khanewal, Mianwali, Dera Ghazi Khan), southern Sindh along the Indus, western Balochistan
arid to semi-arid; summers up to 50 C
Prosopis cineraria (jhand, kandi), Salvadora oleoides (peelu, wan), Capparis aphylla (karir), Vachellia nilotica (kikar)
camels, houbara bustard, chinkara, golden jackal, Balochistan gerbil, porcupines and rattlesnakes
heavily degraded: most of these natural jungles cleared for settlements and canal-irrigated farming
